correctness.rationale: The fixed-degree calculation checks from first principles. Complex Haar source weights are Dirichlet(1,...,1), so after cancellation of the common exponential denominator the CG minimum is a smooth function of finitely many weighted empirical moments. For Y=(n/j)^p, their deterministic means have o(n^-1/2) bias through order 2d+1 exactly under (4d+2)p<1, and the centered triangular array satisfies a multivariate Lindeberg CLT with covariance 1/[1-(a+b)p]. The transformed minimization is the monic shifted-Jacobi problem with weight x^(p^-1-2d-2); its leading coefficient and norm give F_d=binom(p^-1-2,d)^(-2). The envelope derivative is (1-p)Y(r_d(Y)^2-F_d), whose L2 norm gives the displayed variance. Real Haar weights have variance two, doubling the Gaussian variance. Finally F_{d-1}>F_d>F_{d+1}, and the same hypothesis places d+1 in the finite-moment regime, so the CLT at the exact threshold yields the 1/2-1/2 stopping law.

originality.rationale: Chen et al. analyze the fixed-parameter CG/RCD phase diagram and finite-degree floors for the same Haar power-law source model, but the located v1 does not state an interior fixed-degree sqrt(n) fluctuation theorem or a critical tolerance two-point stopping law. Paquette-Trogdon prove CG fluctuation results for sample-covariance ensembles, and Velikanov-Yarotsky develop Jacobi/power-law convergence machinery, but neither covers this deterministic power-law spectrum with Haar source weights and the exact F_d stopping threshold. The submitted theorem therefore fills a distinct fluctuation regime rather than merely renaming an existing CLT.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem upgrades deterministic fixed-degree floors to a quantitative stochastic transition law, including an explicit variance and an exact limiting iteration-count mixture at the critical tolerance. This clarifies the finite-size behavior precisely at the phase boundaries that first-order CG/RCD comparisons leave unresolved and provides a tractable baseline for the variance-critical and heavy-tail regimes.

limitations: The theorem is fixed degree and requires the strict finite-variance condition (4d+2)p<1.
It does not address the variance-critical boundary, heavier tails, growing degree, preconditioning, or finite precision.
The originality conclusion is model- and threshold-specific; broad CG fluctuation theory already exists in other ensembles.
